**Risk level: Amber** – we’re handling payments and private data, so 📦 Supabase Auth, Stripe, and server‑side checks are required. --- ## Short answer > No. Checking `user.isPro` on the frontend is **not safe**. Anyone who can open the browser dev tools could fake that value and see the paid content. We need a server‑side (Edge or API route) that: 1. stores the real `is_pro` flag in Supabase, 2. serves paid pages only when the flag is true, and 3. flips the flag **only after receiving a signed webhook** from Stripe. --- ### What we’ll do, step‑by‑step | Step | What to do | Why it matters | Proof we’ll get it working | |------|------------|----------------|---------------------------| | **1** | Create a new Supabase table `subscriptions` with columns: `user_id`, `stripe_customer_id`, `is_pro` (boolean). | Keeps the paid status in the database – cannot be faked. | After migration we’ll see the table and the correct columns in Supabase. | | **2** | Add a Row‑Level Security (RLS) policy so only the user or a trusted admin can read their own row. | Prevents other users from seeing each other’s paid status. | Policy appears in Supabase “Auth” tab, “Row Level Security” section. | | **3** | Write a Supabase Edge function (`/api/check-pro`) that:
• reads the auth token from the request
• fetches the `is_pro` flag from the `subscriptions` table
• returns `{"isPro": true/false}`. | All checks happen server‑side, so the client can’t cheat. | Call the endpoint from a Postman request; we’ll see the JSON payload. | | **4** | Add a Stripe Checkout session → `/api/checkout`. It’ll create a Checkout Session, save the `stripe_customer_id` to `subscriptions`. | We start the payment flow correctly. | On successful checkout we’ll see a new row in `subscriptions`. | | **5** | Create a Stripe webhook listener (`/api/stripe-webhook`) that:
• verifies the Stripe signature
• when the event is `invoice.payment_succeeded`, sets `is_pro = true` in `subscriptions`. | Only the real Stripe payment can flip the flag. | After a real test payment, the `is_pro` value updates in the DB. | | **6** | In the Next.js app, replace any `user.isPro` checks with a call to `/api/check-pro`. Wrap the paid pages in a `RequirePro` component that fetches that flag and redirects if false. | The frontend **never** trusts its own data. | The paid page loads only after the API response comes back `true`. | | **7** | Add a period‑in‑time check: if `is_pro` is true but the Stripe subscription is past‑due or cancelled, set `is_pro` back to false. | Keeps access in sync with the real subscription status. | We’ll test by cancelling a subscription in Stripe and watching the flag reset. | | **8** | (Optional) Put a simple `isPro` guard on the server‑side data fetches (e.g., in `getServerSideProps`). | Even if someone bypasses the UI, the data still stays protected. | If we try to fetch protected data as a non‑pro, the server returns 403. | --- ## What you need to set up | Item | How to do it | |------|--------------| | Stripe account | Sign up at stripe.com | | Stripe secret key | Add it to your `.env.local` and to Replit/Cursor secrets. Prefix with `STRIPE_` (no `NEXT_PUBLIC_`). | | Supabase project | Create a project, enable Auth, copy the `anon` key (public, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`) and `service_role` key (only for server functions). | | Cursor secrets | Store `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. | | Node.js runtime | Cursor supports it, so the API routes will run in “Functions” or “Edge Functions”. | --- ## Do you want me to draft the code snippets? Just tell me the name of the Next.js folder where you want the API routes (e.g., `app/api`) and I’ll paste the exact files. Or if you prefer, I can walk you through each file touch‑by‑touch. --- **Quick sanity check for you** > *Will a paid user see the content after we’ve set everything up?* > ✅ **Yes** – the `RequirePro` component will query `/api/check-pro`, get `true`, and render the paid page. > *Can a non‑paid user fake `isPro = true`?* > ❌ **No** – they would have to call the private Stripe webhook endpoint, which is protected by the signature check. Let me know which step you'd like to tackle first or if any of the terminology needs more explanation!
